newsitem.title: MOZAMBIQUE: Chissano says Mozambique economy showing progress.
newsitem.headline: Chissano says Mozambique economy showing progress.

text.p: Mozambique's economy was making good progress under the government's austerity policy, President Joaquim Chissano said on Monday.

Chissano told parliament in a state-of-the-nation address that 1996 had produced "tangible advances" in the economy, with growth in gross domestic product of about six percent and a leap in commodity exports of 24 percent.
Inflation fell to 16.6 percent last year from 54 percent in 1995.

The government had stuck to its austerity policy, strictly controlling public expenditure and allowing banks to extend credit to the private sector "without producing inflationary pressures", he said.

Chissano said 1996 was "a year rich in political, economic and social achievements", with statistics showing increased life expectancy, an increase in the number of schools in operation and expansion of the country's health network.
Good rains and an increased grain harvest helped to reduce dependence on imports, he said.
Mozambique has enjoyed an economic revival since the end of a civil war which raged between 1976 and 1992.
Chissano said there had been an alarming increase in crime in Mozambique last year and criminals were becoming more sophisticated.
"Some policemen have succumbed to bribes and some have even worked hand in glove with criminals. A lot still needs to be done to make our police a credible force," he said.
